_comment: MCP server config loaded and ${VAR:-default}-expanded in-process by agent/harness/mcp/config.ts (TruthCV's own harness, no external CLI) in agent/Dockerfile's image (see docker-compose.yml `agent` service). Plain JSON has no comment syntax, so notes live in these _comment keys instead — the config loader ignores unknown keys, and the sibling Jobs project's docker/mcp.json (heavily-commented everywhere else) is itself comment-free, evidence the same convention already held there. ${VAR:-default} below is expanded by agent/harness/mcp/config.ts in-process; it reads this container's actual environment (docker-compose.yml `agent` service), so it stays correct if either default ever changes there.

truthcv._comment: TruthCV's own tool surface: generate_cover_letter, record_application, record_screening, check_cooldown, get_canonical_cv, get_profile_answers, record_company_board, get_job_profiles, recommend_salary. REST routes at GET /mcp/tools and POST /mcp/tools/{name} (agenttools/server.py) provide HTTP access; JSON-RPC streamable-HTTP endpoint at POST /mcp (registered in api/main.py via Server.streamable_http_app() with json_response=True, stateless_http=True, over the tool registry in agenttools/mcp_app.py) is what this `http` type MCP server calls. The default is the in-network address of the `app` compose service — reachable only from inside the compose network, not from the host or the open internet.

browser._comment: The ONLY browser driver (AGENT_BROWSER_DRIVER=browser). @playwright/mcp serving headful Chromium under Xvfb in the `browser` compose service (browser/Dockerfile, browser/entrypoint.sh). Exposes browser_navigate, browser_click, browser_type, browser_file_upload, browser_snapshot, browser_take_screenshot and the rest of the upstream Playwright MCP tool set. The tool set is now ENUMERATED via the `allowedTools` key above (mirrored in agent/harness/tools.ts's BROWSER_ALLOWED_TOOL_NAMES) rather than granted as a whole server. The default is the in-network address of the `browser` service — reachable only from inside the compose network, not from the host or the open internet. The container keeps a persistent Chromium profile on a named volume, so a one-time manual login through the noVNC viewport, reached from the Agents page → Site sign-ins, survives restarts, and it mounts the app data volume read-only at /app/data so browser_file_upload can resolve the `path` get_canonical_cv returns — reachable only because browser/entrypoint.sh also launches the pinned @playwright/mcp (browser/Dockerfile) with --output-dir covering /app (see browser/README.md 'Data Volume'); the mount alone does not grant that access.

_browserDriverComment: The containerised `browser` service above is the only browser driver. An alternative driver reaching the operator's already-logged-in HOST Chrome, via a stdio MCP server dialing a bind-mounted unix socket to a host daemon, was previously declared here and has been removed deliberately: the containerised browser is self-contained, requires no host state, and is what CI and every deployment actually run. AGENT_BROWSER_DRIVER (docker-compose.yml `agent` service) is retained as a validating one-value switch so a second driver can be added here again in the future without every call site needing to change.
